title: quantization-nan-debug-scratchpad-maya-2026-03-18
content:
Goal:
- Triage NaN/quality regression observed after int8 conversion of gpt-like model (gpt-small-v2 candidate).

Observed behavior:
- After PTQ int8 conversion (per-channel, 8-bit symmetric) some prompts produce immediate NaN logits / loss during evaluation.
- Repro: recipe/int8-calibrate.py -> convert -> eval_perplexity.py on eval-subset.
- Example: eval run at 2026-03-17T22:14Z: first batch ok, second batch loss -> NaN, logits contain `inf`/`nan`.
- Quick metrics: FP32 baseline ppl=23.2, BF16 baseline ppl=23.5, INT8 run ppl=NaN (drop-in failure).

Environment:
- GPU: A100 40GB (driver 535.54), CUDA 12.1, pytorch 2.2.0, triton 2.1, bitsandbytes 0.41.0, transformers 4.36, safetensors 0.3.3
- Conversion script: tools/quantize/ptq_convert.py (uses huggingface linear-quantize hooks + custom kernel selection).

Commands tried (most relevant):
1) Convert with per-channel symmetric int8 + calibrate on 2k samples:
   python tools/quantize/ptq_convert.py --model-dir models/gpt-small-v2 --out models/gpt-small-v2-int8 --calibrate-dataset data/calib-2k --per-channel --clip 6.0

2) Eval:
   python eval/eval_perplexity.py --model models/gpt-small-v2-int8 --data data/eval-subset --batch-size 8

3) Quick isolate: run single prompt in interactive python loop to watch activations:
   python - <<EOF
import torch, transformers
model = transformers.AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained('models/gpt-small-v2-int8')
input_ids = torch.tensor([[101, 23, 45]])
with torch.no_grad():
    out = model(input_ids)
    logits = out.logits
    print('logits finite?', torch.isfinite(logits).all())
EOF

Error snippets (captured):
- Runtime snippet from eval: "ValueError: NaN encountered in loss computation"
- Activation check: `logits_finite = False`; printing logits shows `tensor([[[nan, nan, nan, ...]]])`.
- Occasional stack trace: "at linear_cuda_kernel.cu: softmax produced inf (overflow) -> upstream results in loss nan" (this is paraphrased from device log).

Hypotheses so far:
- Hypothesis A: asymmetric range/clipping mismatch during conversion -> some weights or biases get quantized to extreme values -> softmax overflow.
- Hypothesis B: per-tensor vs per-channel scaling mismatch between linear and layernorm ops (casts in wrong order).
- Hypothesis C: kernel implementation bug for int8 matmul on specific sequence lengths (edge-case causing overflow to inf).
- Hypothesis D: calibration dataset not representative -> some embedding rows saturate -> catastrophic activations for certain token IDs.

Quick experiments & outcomes:
- Experiment 1 (sanity): load FP32 model, run same prompt -> logits finite (ok). Suggests conversion step introduces issue.
- Experiment 2 (BF16): convert model to BF16 and eval -> ppl ~ baseline, no NaNs. So cast path is fine for BF16.
- Experiment 3 (INT8 per-tensor): convert with per-tensor (no per-channel) -> still NaN, but failure modes differ (NaN appears slightly later in sequence).
- Experiment 4 (remove bias quantization): quantize weights only, keep biases FP32 -> still NaN but less frequent.
- Experiment 5 (increase clip threshold to 8.0): redo calibration -> still NaN.
- Experiment 6 (freeze layernorm to FP32): keep layernorm & embedding in FP32, quantize rest -> model stable (no NaN) in ~80% cases. This points to numerical instability around layernorm/cast boundaries.

Notable observations:
- When layernorm stays FP32, NaNs mostly disappear.
- NaNs are correlated with tokens that lead to very peaky attention (long tail tokens).
- Intermediate debug: printing pre-softmax attention scores shows extremely large positive numbers (e.g. 1e9) before softmax -> then softmax returns 1.0 for one position and 0 for others -> downstream logs show divide-by-zero/inf in next ops.

Stack / log excerpt (raw-ish):
  forward aten::matmul -> aten::addmm -> linear_quantized_kernel_int8 (custom)
  WARNING: kernel output contains inf at index [0,5,12]
  Loss: nan (backprop aborted)

Potential root causes to prioritize:
- Layernorm quantization/cast ordering: ensure residual add + layernorm compute in consistent dtype to avoid mixing quantized inputs with FP32 stats. (Exp 6 supports this).
- Quantized bias handling: biases should be dequantized before add; check code path in ptq_convert.py.
- Kernel overflow: check int8 GEMM kernel implementation for accumulation dtype. Accumulation must be int32/float32; if using int8->int8 accumulate with low precision, may overflow.
- Softmax implementation: confirm softmax uses numerically-stable max-subtract trick (it does in FP32 but maybe not in custom int8 path).

Next steps / TODOs:
- [ ] Add assert checks in conversion: verify per-layer scales are finite and not zero/inf after calibration. Dump scales.json per layer.
- [ ] Re-run calibration with longer, stratified dataset (include rare tokens).
- [ ] Force layernorm & attention softmax to FP32 path (temporary mitigation) and re-run suite.
- [ ] Add unit test: random inputs -> forward -> check isfinite for logits (CI gate for quantized kernels).
- [ ] Audit linear kernel accum dtype and softmax impl in custom kernels (triton files under kernels/).
- [ ] Try alternative quantization scheme: GPTQ-like asymmetric per-channel + outlier handling.
- [ ] Compare activation histograms (FP32 vs INT8) for failing prompts to identify extreme activations.

Experiment notes (IDs):
- exp/int8/2026-03-17-01 (per-channel, clip6) -> fail
- exp/int8/2026-03-17-02 (layernorm FP32) -> partial success

Useful quick checks to run now:
- dump scales: python tools/quantize/dump_scales.py --model models/gpt-small-v2-int8 --out tmp/scales.json
- run per-layer activation probe: python tools/debug/activation_probe.py --layer 5 --prompt "<failing prompt>" --model models/gpt-small-v2-int8

Notes to self (less formal):
- Might be a casting order bug introduced when we optimized quantize->fuse passes last quarter. Lee suspected layernorm fusion change around PR #772.
- Devon: check bitsandbytes kernel versions; earlier bnb bug gave inf with dynamic quantization on A100 (search slack convo #infra-gpu).
- If cannot fix quickly, fallback for Dedicated customers: use BF16 profile + note cost tradeoff.

References / breadcrumbs:
- Slack: #quantization thread 2026-03-17 (Maya -> Lee)
- PR: github:reddwarf/llm-inference#772 (layernorm fusion changes)
- Jira: RED-5231 (customer report), RED-5302 (kernel audit)

If I get a reliable small repro (single prompt that deterministically triggers NaN) then escalate to kernels team with explicit inputs + minimal model snapshot.

Scratch / quick checklist of things I actually did (timestamps local):
- 2026-03-17 19:02 ran calib 2k -> created models/gpt-small-v2-int8 (files written)
- 2026-03-17 21:30 first NaN observed in eval queue
- 2026-03-17 22:05 manual interactive test -> confirmed logits contain NaN before loss
- 2026-03-17 22:40 exp: layernorm FP32 -> reduction in NaN instances

Final quick note: highest probability cause = layernorm + quantized linear interaction / cast ordering. Prioritize audit of convert step and triton kernel accumulation dtype.

-- M.S.
